spec_match.rationale: Runs the real requestDevice -> gatt.connect flow behind a user gesture, reads server.maxWriteWithoutResponseSize, listens for maxwritewithoutresponsesizechanged, and feature-detects on the prototype rather than an instance — with the reasoning for that documented in the page and matching the conformance suite.

interactive.rationale: A four-tile capability readout populates at load, and pair/disconnect buttons drive a real GATT connection with a live log, size readout, a vs-20-bytes ratio and a change counter.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises the real requestDevice flow plus 'the honest unsupported branch when the API, the adapter, or the permission is not there' — and that honest branch is exactly what this session observed.

edge_cases.rationale: NotFoundError from a dismissed chooser is logged as a normal outcome, gattserverdisconnected restores button state, getAvailability failure is reported as 'query failed', insecure context and missing-API each get specific explanatory copy, and the pair button disables when pairing cannot work.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5177569273053184 and the Web Bluetooth spec.

conformance.rationale: The suite is mostly excellent (prototype presence, readonly-accessor descriptor check, EventTarget inheritance, promptless availability), and its 1 pass / 7 fail run here is the honest result for a build with no navigator.bluetooth at all — but the requestdevice-requires-a-user-gesture assertion passed on this API-less build for the wrong reason, flagged below.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 on Linux (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) has no navigator.bluetooth, so the genuinely observed behaviour is the degradation path: console logged 'api=false property=false secure=true adapter=unknown' and the screenshots show the rose not-available banner, absent/absent/yes/unknown tiles, the correct explanatory note and a disabled pair button; the pairing flow itself needs real hardware and is judged from wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert covers the support probe (observed at load), connection, size changes, and pair failures by error name; console carries only the page's labelled logs.

design_system.rationale: Variables and button overrides are correct and the observed rose banner passes AA (~4.8:1), but the .support.yes state uses --accent-emerald on stone (~3.7:1), the recurring shared-palette shortfall, for its bold normal-size text.

accessibility.rationale: The log is an aria-live=polite list with an aria-label, capability and result readouts are definition lists, the banner pairs an aria-hidden icon with text, and buttons carry clear names and disabled states.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px and 1280px: tiles stack to one column, the banner wraps, and there is no horizontal overflow or clipped control on either class.

openQuestions.title: FLAG FOR HUMAN: user-gesture assertion passes on builds with no Web Bluetooth at all
openQuestions.detail: conformance.json's 'requestdevice-requires-a-user-gesture' catches any DOMException or TypeError from awaiting navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice(...). On this build navigator.bluetooth is undefined, so the await throws TypeError from the property access and the assertion PASSES — observed live in this session's 1-pass/7-fail run — without proving anything about user activation. A guard like requiring navigator.bluetooth to exist first (returning false or blocked otherwise) would make it meaningful, but the suite is immutable: flagging for a human per the conformance policy, not editing.

openQuestions.title: Adapter tile could drive the support verdict too
openQuestions.detail: The ready verdict is hasApi && hasProperty && secure; adapter='no' only softens the note text while the banner would still read as supported on a 157+ build with no adapter. Folding a definitive adapter 'no' into the banner (or a third 'present but no adapter' state) would make the top-line verdict match the tiles in that configuration.

summary: The capability-honesty anchor of this feature's portfolio, and it proved itself in this session: headless Linux Chromium 141 exposes no navigator.bluetooth, and the page reported exactly that — rose 'not available here' banner, absent/absent/yes/unknown tiles, the right explanatory note naming iOS/Linux/iframe causes, and a disabled pair button, with console clean. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v157/web-bluetooth-bluetoothremotegattserver-maxwritewithoutresponsesize/mtu-probe/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots, DOM dump; feature /conformance/ route 1 pass / 7 fail, the honest result for an API-less build). Real pairing requires hardware and was judged from wiring, which handles dismissal, disconnection and availability failures correctly. One suite-level flag: the user-gesture assertion's observed pass here is vacuous, since it cannot distinguish gesture enforcement from a missing API.
